messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [redacted]

Age: 56 years

Gender: Male

Admission Date: [redacted]

Discharge Date: [redacted]
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with subjective fever, body aches, nonproductive cough, left-sided pleuritic chest pain, and recurrent infected skin cyst with MRSA. Physical examination revealed coarse breath sounds with no wheezing, and a thick purulence was exposed from the cyst. Radiographic and CT studies showed developments of multifocal regions of nodular appearing infiltration within both lungs. Blood culture resulted in positive with MRSA that grew with different antibiotic sensitivities. Despite being on the antibiotic/vancomycin, the patient continued to be bacteremic with MRSA, and repeated chest CT scan revealed the progression of lung pneumonia and multiple new nodules. Further TEE revealed a large vegetation was involving the pulmonic valve that was adherent to the artery itself. The patient underwent pulmonary valve replacement using a LivaNova extra-large sutureless valve. Tissue valve culture came back positive for MRSA, and the patient was discharged home on IV vancomycin for six weeks.

Hospital Course Summary:
The patient was admitted with a history of recurrent infected skin cyst with MRSA, subjective fever, body aches, nonproductive cough, and left-sided pleuritic chest pain. Workup revealed MRSA Pulmonary Valve Endocarditis, and the patient underwent a pulmonary valve replacement. After a total of six weeks of IV vancomycin therapy, the patient was discharged home.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this admission is acute MRSA infective endocarditis of the pulmonic valve, which caused the persistent bacteraemia and septic lung nodules and required valve replacement. This is a circulatory system condition in chapter I. Acute and subacute infective endocarditis is classified to I33 (I33.0) rather than the non-infective pulmonary valve category I37.

CODE: I33
